title: Short Stuff: Death from Astral Projection
summary: Short Stuff episode on the 1975 death of Robert Antosh Chic (spelled Robert Antosh Chick in the hosts' transcript as "Robert and toast Chick"; the hosts also say "Bobby A"), a yoga practitioner from Ann Arbor, Michigan, who had studied yoga in India under Iyengar and was found dead after a multi-day astral projection meditation in June 1975. The hosts cover astral projection and the silver cord belief, the medical examiner's failure to find a cause, the theory that he slowed his heartbeat through yogic meditation, and the official ruling of cocaine overdose, which the hosts find doubtful given his lifestyle and lack of evidence. The episode ends with a shout-out to a Medium article on the history of astral projection.

segments.title: Opening banter
segments.summary: Hosts joke about being in spirit and on the astral plane, then introduce the story of Robert Antosh Chick, a yoga teacher in Ann Arbor who studied in India.

segments.title: Robert Antosh Chick's background and astral projection
segments.summary: Robert Antosh Chick, a vegetarian former Marine and yoga teacher, studied esoteric yoga under Iyengar in India in the 1970s. The hosts explain astral projection as a meditation technique focused on the line between sleep and wakefulness, and describe the silver cord that tethers the spirit to the body.

segments.title: Silver cord severance and the belief in being lost
segments.summary: The hosts describe the belief that the silver cord is severed at death, or accidentally, leaving the spirit permanently lost in the astral plane, and say believers make a case that this happened to Robert.

segments.title: Discovery of Robert's body in June 1975
segments.summary: In June 1975, Robert told his roommates he would meditate and astral project, hanging a sign on his door. After several days, roommates found him dead in a meditative pose, with a serene expression on his face.

segments.title: Medical examiner finds no cause of death
segments.summary: The medical examiner's autopsy found no injury or disease, and he said he could not even guess a cause. Undigested food in the stomach suggested death soon after the Sunday meditation. Quincy was also mentioned as having no answer.

segments.title: Theory of yogic heartbeat slowing
segments.summary: The medical examiner considered that Robert may have slowed his heartbeat to a stop through yogic meditation. The hosts discuss claims of yogis controlling heart rate, note that it is not well verified, and say astral projection is considered dangerous in yoga.

segments.title: Official cocaine overdose ruling and doubts
segments.summary: The official cause of death was ruled a cocaine overdose, which the hosts and family found surprising given Robert's clean living. The hosts discuss cocaine use in the 1970s and say no explanation for the ruling can be found.

segments.title: Closing thoughts and sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts describe the possible fate of the lost spirit and mention a Medium article by Nick Repasitrony on the history of astral projection, then sign off.
